title: Same Bench dialogue options
about: This page lays out ten writers' versions of the Same Bench dialogue, ranked, and three combined drafts for the whole 14-second short. Nothing in the scene, script or voices has changed yet.

dialogues.label: Same Bench: the whole short
dialogues.where: Beats A (1919, veteran), B (today, nurse), C (the button)
dialogues.target: 14 s or less in total, about 5 + 5 + 4 s

now.line: (he hasn't aged a day; how it lands is open)

drafts.name: Hero. Forget it.
drafts.bet: The joke is thanks and bin in one breath: he praises and dismisses in the same line, and the echo plus a pre-emptive third dismissal says same man.

lines.line: [hat in hand] Sir, about my pension...
[not looking up] Hero. Forget it.
[veteran's crutch slides; he stands and goes]
Today.
[tired, lanyard in hand] Sir, about my pay...
[same pose, same paper] Hero. Forget it.
[she looks at her pay slip and goes]
[a third shadow falls across his paper; he does not look up] Forget it.
Same bench.

notes: Trim: drop the Today. caption if the nurse's scrubs read at once; drop 'Same bench.' if the third Forget it lands as the button.
Protected 'Forget it.' kept verbatim three times; 'Hero.' is a tag Jack can cut without loss.
Risk: the pension and pay asks must be dry, not pleading. 'Pay' stays generic: no dates, no governments. Muted autoplay is covered by the captions.

drafts.name: The plaque and the tip
drafts.bet: The picture and one object do the arguing: a plaque begging the park to remember under a man telling people to forget, so only two spoken words are needed.

lines.line: [pats the brass plaque on the bench back: LEST WE FORGET. PRESENTED BY THE WHALEBY TRUST] Forget it.
[veteran with pinned trouser leg stands and goes; a WELCOME HOME bunting scrap on the ground]
Now.
[same pat, same paper, same flick of the hand] Forget it.
[nurse goes; a second plate under the first: THANK YOU HEROES]
[he lowers the paper and tips his hat to camera; one page-turn, one dry brass tink]
Same bench.

notes: Trim: lose the THANK YOU HEROES plate if the frame is too small to read at 9:16; hold each plaque 1.5 s minimum.
Protected 'Forget it.' kept twice, only stage directions added. Whaleby Trust is invented; check it names no real body.
Risk: lives or dies on the drawing matching frame for frame; thin if Jack wants a spoken button. Alt button: he says 'Next.' to a sketch outline at the park gate.

drafts.name: Quick learner
drafts.bet: The nurse knows his line before he says it, so the audience gets there first and his delight at it is the whole indictment.

lines.line: [hopeful] They said I'd be seen right, sir...
[not looking up from his paper] Forget it.
[veteran goes]
Today.
[sits, flinches, mouths it flat, quoting him] Forget it.
[delighted, same paper] Forget it. Quick learner.
[she gets up and goes; his face unchanged]
[a shadow falls; he lowers the paper an inch] Forget it.
NEXT.

notes: Trim: 'Quick learner.' can go, leaving the pre-emption alone; shorten the veteran to 'They said I'd be seen right, sir.'
Protected 'Forget it.' kept verbatim; also spoken by the nurse as a quote.
Risk: the nurse saying it can read as her forgetting, so the flinch must show she is quoting him. Cut-off asks are hard for TTS; the nurse line may need sound design.

ranking.verdict: Best fit: 'Hero. Forget it.' carries thanked-then-forgotten in four syllables and keeps him the target. Fails on density (three captions) and 'Same man. Same bill.' edges toward a stated moral.
Tightest mechanism: he interrupts, then fires on a shadow, so the button is the rule itself. Fails on 'NEXT.' possibly reading as a queue joke, and cut-off lines are hard to voice.
The cleverest single idea (plaque plus his name) and fully unstated. Fails on legibility at 9:16 and on being funny aloud; has no resistance from the victims.
Genuine reversal and a dark 'Quick learner'. Fails because the nurse saying 'Forget it' can blame the carer, and the extra line risks sermon.
Right instinct (the picture says it) and short. Fails on thin voices and on muted-feed readability; the button options are a menu, not a decision.
On target and unstated, but three flat reads feel lazy and 'thanked' relies wholly on art. No resistance, no character voices.
Only shape with real pushback and a dark 'Keep the leg, then'. Fails: victims bargaining themselves down puts the weight on them, not on him, and 'A clap?' is too knowing.
Good craft (match cut, hat tip) but the sincere 'They said...' pleas are copied one-for-one and the hat tip is ambiguous.
Pigeons say 'Same bloke. Same bench.', so the chorus states the point and twee voices soften the dark. Costs two extra voices.
Fails the brief: 'You were useful. Now you're not.' is a lecture, and 'Works every time.' is the moral spoken aloud.

1A: Forget it. (x3, 'Hero.' added in A and B)

questions.text: Do you want any words beyond 'Forget it.'? 1A adds 'Hero.' and the asks, 1B adds none, 1C adds the veteran's plea and 'Quick learner.'
Spoken button, caption or silent? 1A and 1C fire a third 'Forget it.' at a stranger, 1B ends on a silent hat tip and a caption.
Should the nurse and veteran speak at all, or stay silent so only he has a voice?
Is a closing caption ('Same bench.' / 'NEXT.') allowed, or does that tip into stating the moral?
1B needs a plaque readable at 9:16 and a frame-identical second drawing. Is the art budget there for it?
